comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers infrastructure and security software to simplify IT environments, support hybrid cloud platforms, and manage mission-critical workloads for Fortune 500 companies and government agencies, including fibre channel storage networking products.
comparisons.comparison: Both QCOM and AVGO explicitly identify government agencies as customers for their respective businesses. QCOM's nonreportable QGOV segment sells products and services directly to U.S. government agencies (qcom_2024_1_P049_S003). Similarly, AVGO’s infrastructure software solutions are relied upon by government agencies to manage on-premises and hybrid cloud environments (avgo_2024_1_P003_S002).

sentences.text: QGOV provides development and other services and sells related products to U.S. government agencies and their contractors.

Many of the largest companies in the world, including most of the Fortune 500, and many government agencies rely on our software solutions to help manage and secure their on-premises and hybrid cloud environments, private cloud infrastructure and AI data centers.

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, the company began shipping Micron G9 TLC based NAND in SSDs designed for low-latency, high-throughput workloads including AI training, machine learning, and cloud computing.
comparisons.comparison: QCOM discloses a cloud computing processing initiative as a nonreportable segment, while MU describes specific products (G9 TLC based NAND SSDs) designed for cloud computing workloads. Both disclosures address the company's involvement in cloud computing, but QCOM treats it as an internal business unit/initiative, whereas MU details the specific memory technology sold to support cloud infrastructure.
